messages.author: e4aec126ff1dca22
messages.subject: ggmap 2.3 released
parts:
Hi all –

The new version of ggmap fixes several of the longstanding issues.  There are still many things to be implemented!  Hopefully I'll get some time this summer to implement some of these.  Thanks to all who have made suggestions (I haven't forgotten them!).

Cheers
david.

If you're not familiar with ggmap, here's a sample of ggmap on a random recent ggplot2 spatial question. 

library(maps)
library(ggplot2)
library(plyr)

# make fake choropleth data
texas <- map("county", regions = "texas", plot = FALSE, fill = TRUE)
texas <- fortify(texas)
texas <- ddply(texas, "subregion", function(df){
  mutate(df, fake = rnorm(1))
})

# make standard ggplot map (without geom_map)
qplot(long, lat, data = texas, geom = "polygon", 
  group = group, colour = I("white"), fill = fake, size = I(.3)
)


# using ggmap...
library(ggmap)
(p <- qmap('texas', zoom = 6, maptype = 'satellite', legend = 'topleft') +
  geom_polygon(
    aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group, fill = fake), data = texas,
    color = 'white', alpha = .75, size = .2
  ))

  

# and a little pizazz...
cities <- c('houston', 'san antonio', 'waco', 'dallas', 'austin', 'el paso',
  'abilene', 'amarillo', 'brownsville', 'plano', 'galveston')
cities_locs <- geocode(cities)
cities_locs$city <- cities 
p + geom_text(aes(label = city), data = cities_locs, color = 'yellow', size = 3)




-------------------------------------------------------------
-------------------------------------------------------------

From: David Kahle <david...@gmail.com>
To: ggplot2 <ggp...@googlegroups.com>
Sent: Monday, April 15, 2013 12:50 PM
Subject: ggmap 2.3 released

Hi all –

The new version of ggmap fixes several of the longstanding issues.  There are still many things to be implemented!  Hopefully I'll get some time this summer to implement some of these.  Thanks to all who have made suggestions (I haven't forgotten them!).

Cheers
david.

If you're not familiar with ggmap, here's a sample of ggmap on a random recent ggplot2 spatial question. 

library(maps)
library(ggplot2)
library(plyr)

# make fake choropleth data
texas <- map("county", regions = "texas", plot = FALSE, fill = TRUE)
texas <- fortify(texas)
texas <- ddply(texas, "subregion", function(df){
  mutate(df, fake = rnorm(1))
})

# make standard ggplot map (without geom_map)
qplot(long, lat, data = texas, geom = "polygon", 
  group = group, colour = I("white"), fill = fake, size = I(.3)
)


# using ggmap...
library(ggmap)
(p <- qmap('texas', zoom = 6, maptype = 'satellite', legend = 'topleft') +
  geom_polygon(
    aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group, fill = fake), data = texas,
    color = 'white', alpha = .75, size = .2
  ))
  
# and a little pizazz...
cities <- c('houston', 'san antonio', 'waco', 'dallas', 'austin', 'el paso',
  'abilene', 'amarillo', 'brownsville', 'plano', 'galveston')
cities_locs <- geocode(cities)
cities_locs$city <- cities 
p + geom_text(aes(label = city), data = cities_locs, color = 'yellow', size = 3)
